evidence.observed_failure: HTTP 403 on hosted page requests made directly to localhost without the reverse-proxy Host and X-Forwarded-Proto context required by the hosted-origin guard
evidence.runtime_logs: service started normally in hosted-staging mode with WFM_PUBLIC_ORIGIN=https://wfm-ci.invalid

root_cause.description: The CI proof container was intentionally configured with an HTTPS public origin, but the HTTP harness called 127.0.0.1 without modelling the trusted reverse-proxy request context. The application's hosted-origin guard therefore correctly rejected the requests.

resolution.change: Customer-proof HTTP probes now send Host: wfm-ci.invalid and X-Forwarded-Proto: https while retaining the HTTPS origin guard.
resolution.verification: The exact subsequent Customer Proof Gate run 35230273480 passed all steps including hosted HTTP boundary.

permanent_prevention.rule: Any isolated hosted-staging proof that configures an HTTPS WFM_PUBLIC_ORIGIN must model the same reverse-proxy host/protocol context expected in the deployed environment; never weaken the application origin guard to make a local proof pass.
permanent_prevention.failure_classification_requirement: If health identity passes but hosted page probes return 403, first compare proof proxy context with hosted-origin policy before classifying the candidate as a product regression.
permanent_prevention.expected_result: Hosted health, root page, kiosk page and unauthenticated bootstrap boundary all pass using the declared hosted origin context.
